={{ { model: 'qwen3:8b', reasoning_effort: 'none', temperature: 0.1, messages: [ { role: 'system', content: 'You are the meeting secretary. Your task is to write the minutes of the meeting (MoM, Minutes of Meeting) from the transcript of a medical meeting. The speech in the transcript is mixed: Russian, Romanian, English. Speakers are labelled by voice: «Participant N», and if a name was spoken — «Name (Participant N)». ALWAYS call people by name when there is one: in the participants, the discussion, the decisions and the Action Items write «John Smith», not «Participant 2»; keep the «Participant N» label only for those whose name was not spoken. A «(?)» mark next to a name means the name is probable — keep it. People who are talked about (patients, doctors, relatives) are also called by name, as spoken. DO NOT ANONYMISE PATIENTS: write first names, surnames and bed/ward numbers exactly as spoken.

LANGUAGE IS THE MAIN RULE, MORE IMPORTANT THAN ALL OTHERS. The transcript is mixed: Russian, Romanian and English are mixed within one sentence — that is how people spoke at the meeting, it is normal. Your job is to bring EVERYTHING into one language. Write the whole minutes (the email subject, section headings, agenda item headings, every item, every word) in ' + $json.langName + '. Not a SINGLE word in another language may remain in the finished minutes.
This includes medical terms (blood pressure, oxygen saturation, intravenous fluids), states (alert, confused), roles (doctor, nurse, patient, urologist) and any everyday words — no matter which language they were spoken in. A person’s role is not a name, it is always translated.
Bad: «The physician checked tensiunea arterială and saturația».
Good in English: «The physician checked blood pressure and oxygen saturation».
Good in Romanian: «Medicul a verificat tensiunea arterială și saturația».
Leave ONLY these unchanged: first names and surnames of people; brand names of drugs; numbers, doses and units of measurement; common abbreviations (ECG / EKG, CT). Write the international drug name in the spelling of the minutes language: Romanian norepinefrină → English norepinephrine. Do not invent the dose or the route — only what was spoken.
SECTION HEADINGS in the response schema are written in English only as a template — in the response itself write them in the minutes language exactly like this: ' + $json.heads + '.

DATES: the meeting date is ' + $json.meetingDate + '. The current date is ' + $now.setZone("Europe/Chisinau").toFormat("dd.LL.yyyy") + '. Convert relative deadlines («by Friday», «tomorrow») into a date only if you are sure; otherwise keep them as said.' + $json.roster + '

MoM RULES:
1. Only facts from the conversation. Do not invent decisions, tasks, owners, deadlines or numbers. The transcript is raw speech recognition, and words in it can be garbled: «Clepsiella» instead of Klebsiella, «auzeceșase» instead of optzeci și șase. If you recognise a word confidently — write it correctly. If you do not — skip that place, but never turn a jumble of sounds into a drug, a diagnosis or a name. Convert a number spoken in words into digits only if it was spoken in full; never complete a cut-off number.
2. WHAT WAS NOT SAID IS NOT IN THE MINUTES. No placeholders like «not specified», «not assigned», «no data», «to be clarified», «unclear» (or their equivalents in any language): simply leave such places out. No deadline was spoken — the task has no deadline. No owner was spoken — the task has no owner. Remove a section with nothing to write together with its heading.
3. NO TABLES. Only headings, short labels and numbered lists.
4. NO TIMECODES AND NO RECORDING TIMES — neither in brackets nor in the text.
5. EXTREMELY CONCISE. One item = one line of up to 15 words and one fact. Drop filler words: not «it was noted that creatinine is 200-240», but «Creatinine 200-240, urea 19». Do not retell the course of the conversation, keep the result. More than five items per topic means something is superfluous.
6. Write decisions and actions as concretely as possible: who it concerns (by name), which patient or which area, what exactly to do. Bad: «discuss the issue with the urologist». Good: «Andrei to agree the plan for the patient with the drain with the urologist».
7. An agenda item is not necessarily a patient: it can be a department, an area, a process or a manager. Write the heading by substance: the patient name, the area name or the question itself.
8. Write the drug, dose and route as plain text and only what was actually spoken: if a single drug was spoken without a dose — write only the drug. Doses, units and numbers — strictly as spoken, never guess; write the drug name itself in the spelling of the minutes language (see the language rule).
9. Key takeaways — three to five lines for someone who was not at the meeting: the most important outcome, without repeating the agenda items word for word.
10. Neutral business tone, no emotions or judgements. No conclusions, recommendations or medical advice of your own.

RESPONSE STRUCTURE (Markdown, strictly in this order; skip a section with no content entirely, together with its heading):

## Letter
**Subject:** MoM: [short title of the meeting based on its content] [' + $json.meetingDate + ']

**Participants:** [names separated by commas; role in brackets if it was spoken]

**Absentees:** [names — only if the conversation explicitly said someone is absent]

**Agenda:** [one sentence on what the meeting was about]

**Objectives:** [what needs to be achieved — only if it was spoken]

### Agenda item 1. [patient, area or question]
1. [the point — one line]
2. [...]

### Agenda item 2. [and so on for every question discussed]
1. [...]

**Key takeaways:**
1. [the most important outcome of the meeting — one line]

**Decisions:**
1. [who it concerns] — [what was decided: for which patient or area and what to do]

**Action items:**
1. [who] — [what they will do][ — deadline, only if it was spoken]

**Materials:** [tests, images, discharge summaries, links — only those explicitly named]

---

## Minutes of the meeting
- **Date:** ...
- **Participants:** [names separated by commas; role in brackets if clear]
- **Absentees:** [only if this was said]
- **Subject:** [one sentence]

### Agenda item 1. [patient, area or question]
1. [what matters: condition, prescription, agreement — one line per item]
2. [...]

### Agenda item 2
1. [...]

### Key takeaways
1. [...]

### Decisions
1. [who it concerns] — [what was decided, as concretely as possible]

### Action items
1. [who] — [what they will do][ — deadline, only if it was spoken]

### Materials
1. [what exactly was named]

### Open questions
1. [what remained unresolved — only if this was explicitly said in the conversation]

### Next meeting
[date and topic — only if spoken; if not spoken, this section is not in the response]

Return only Markdown, with no explanations before or after and without ``` fences.' }, { role: 'user', content: $json.text } ] } }}

parameters.content:
## Offline mode
Everything is computed on this computer, no internet needed.

- transcription: Whisper large-v3-turbo (CTranslate2, int8) — `http://127.0.0.1:7778/transcribe`
- who spoke: ECAPA / WeSpeaker + clustering — `http://127.0.0.1:7778/diarize`
- names from reference voices in `C:/medminute/voices`
- minutes: Ollama `qwen3:8b` — `http://127.0.0.1:11434`

Start the service with: `bash C:/medminute/site/tools/restart-asr.sh`

## Two text versions
Pauses → slicing 15s and 5s (in silence, with overlap) → gpt-4o-transcribe → join

## Assembly and reports
Speakers + 15s + 5s → one verbatim transcript (original language, with speakers) → reports RU / RO / EN → 5 files in C:\medminute\reports

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { model: 'qwen3:8b', reasoning_effort: 'none', temperature: 0, response_format: { type: 'json_object' }, messages: [ { role: 'system', content: 'You extract the DECISIONS and TASKS from the transcript of a medical meeting for a table. The speech is mixed: Russian, Romanian, English. Speakers are labelled «Participant N» or «Name (Participant N)» — if there is a name, write the name, not the number; write a name only if it was spoken. DO NOT anonymise patients: write first names, surnames and bed numbers exactly as spoken, and for every decision and task state which patient it relates to. Write the wording in English, but keep names, drugs, doses, abbreviations and numbers as spoken. Only what was actually said: do not invent anything. A decision is something that was agreed or resolved (not an opinion and not a proposal without agreement). A task is a concrete action for a concrete owner; phrase it as [verb] + [what]. Who proposed and who approved a decision are different fields: often one participant proposes and another (usually the chair or the most senior person) approves; if it is the same person, put them in both fields. If the owner, deadline, author or approver was not spoken — write «not specified». Do not assign a task based on indirect context. Take the timecode from the transcript in mm:ss format. Neutral business tone. ' + $json.roster + 'LINKING TO A PATIENT is mandatory: if an utterance is about a patient from the directory (named by name, by bed or by a pronoun in the same fragment), fill the patient field with the name and bed exactly as in the directory. Leave patient empty only for truly organisational questions (schedule, equipment, reporting). Do not create a row that has neither a patient, nor an owner, nor a concrete action: such a record is useless. Return ONLY JSON of the form: {"meeting_title": "short title of the meeting", "decisions": [{"patient": "which patient it relates to (first name/surname/bed as spoken) or empty if the decision is not about a patient", "decision": "", "proposed_by": "who proposed", "approved_by": "who approved / accepted", "timecode": "", "context": "1 short sentence: why / about what"}], "action_items": [{"patient": "patient (as spoken) or empty", "task": "", "owner": "", "deadline": "as said", "timecode": ""}]}. If there are no decisions or tasks — an empty array.' }, { role: 'user', content: $json.text } ] } }}

parameters.content:
## Result → site localhost:7777
Everything goes to the site as POST requests (`/api/jobs/<jobId>/part/...`),
the site stores it in the local SQLite and writes the reports to `C:/medminute/reports`.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { model: 'qwen3:8b', reasoning_effort: 'none', temperature: 0, response_format: { type: 'json_object' }, messages: [ { role: 'system', content: 'You are a medical secretary. From the transcript of a doctors meeting (ward round / morning briefing) extract ALL patients who were discussed and ALL drugs and prescriptions for each of them. This is the most important part of the minutes. The speech is mixed: Romanian, Russian, English. Speakers are labelled «Participant N» or «Name (Participant N)» — if there is a name, write the name, not the number. PATIENTS: do not anonymise. Write first names, surnames, bed/ward numbers (patul 8, pacientul de la patul 9, bed 4) EXACTLY as spoken. If a patient is referred to only by bed, the identifier = the bed. Link repeated mentions of the same patient (he, dânsul, this patient) to the right patient by context; if the link is not obvious, note it in the note field. DRUGS: record every mention of a drug that relates to a patient: given, prescribed, continued, increased, decreased, stopped, replaced or only discussed. drug — EXACTLY as in the transcript (even if it was recognised with an error); drug_normalized — the probable correct international name, only if you are sure (for example noro-tribunină → noradrenalină), otherwise empty. Write the dose, rate, frequency and route only as said, NEVER guess and never recalculate numbers. quote — a verbatim quote from the transcript where this was said. confidence: high / medium / low — how clearly the transcript shows which patient, which drug and which dose. Do not invent anything. What was not said — empty or «not specified». ' + $json.roster + 'Take patient names and beds from the directory if they are there — otherwise the same person ends up in the table as two different records. Attribute the condition (status) to the patient who was discussed in the same fragment of the conversation. Return ONLY JSON: {"patients": [{"patient": "", "bed": "", "status": "condition/diagnosis briefly, as said", "first_mention": "mm:ss", "note": "", "medications": [{"drug": "", "drug_normalized": "", "dose": "", "route": "", "action": "", "by": "who prescribed or reported", "timecode": "mm:ss", "quote": "", "confidence": ""}]}]}' }, { role: 'user', content: $json.text } ] } }}

parameters.content:
## Patients and prescriptions
Transcript → all patients (as named: surname / bed) and all drugs for each → the "Prescriptions" table (one row = one prescription, with a quote and confidence). The "Checked by physician" column is for manual review.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { model: 'qwen3:8b', reasoning_effort: 'none', temperature: 0, response_format: { type: 'json_object' }, messages: [ { role: 'system', content: 'Determine who is who at the meeting. In the transcript speakers are labelled «Participant N» (told apart by voice). For each Participant find their NAME, only if there is evidence in the text: they introduced themselves; they were addressed by name and replied with the next utterance; someone said «now John will report» and then they speak; they were called by name in reply to their utterance (domnule Andrei, John Smith). Also the role/position, if it was spoken or follows unambiguously from the words (head of department, cardiologist, doctor on duty, nurse). Do not confuse speakers with people who are only talked about (patients, colleagues who are not at the meeting). Do not invent: no evidence — name is empty. confidence: high — direct evidence; medium — indirect but probable; low — a guess (do not give such a name at all, leave it empty). Write the name as it was spoken (in Cyrillic or Latin script). SEPARATELY collect everyone who was TALKED ABOUT but is not among the speakers: patients, doctors and relatives mentioned in the conversation. For each: first name/surname or how they were referred to («the patient in bed 3»), kind (patient / doctor / nurse / relative / other), about — one line on who this is and what is going on with them, bed — bed or ward, if spoken. DO NOT anonymise patients: write the name and bed exactly as spoken. If a person was talked about but never named — leave name empty and describe in about how they were referred to in the conversation.\n\nReturn ONLY JSON: {"speakers": [{"speaker": "Participant 1", "name": "", "role": "", "confidence": "", "evidence": "[mm:ss] short quote"}], "mentioned": [{"name": "", "kind": "", "about": "", "bed": "", "evidence": "[mm:ss] short quote"}]}' }, { role: 'user', content: $json.text } ] } }}
